h1:
Hat Yai Desserts
Grass Jelly, Shaved Ice & Fresh Coconut
intro: Hat Yai is famous for savory food, but dessert is another reason people will happily stand in line in the sun. The city has old-recipe fresh-coconut sweets, a man-duay stall behind the train station that has been around for over fifty years, rich Southern khanom jeen, and old-school shaved ice for twenty baht a bowl. We picked only the places Hat Yai locals genuinely eat at and that reviews keep mentioning.

blocks.html: Hat Yai desserts have a charm that comes from mixing a few traditions together. There are classic Thai fresh-coconut sweets, Chinese-style shaved ice and grass jelly that have been part of the city for ages, and Southern desserts like coconut-milk khanom jeen that cool you down on a hot day. We rank the dessert and sweet shops by real reviews first, then break down each style and where to go for it.

blocks.text: Hat Yai dessert shops that locals actually visit

blocks.html: This ranking is drawn from shops that reviews mention often and that are still open. The prices listed are rough ranges from reviews and can shift with ingredients and the time of year. We'd suggest double-checking opening hours in a maps app before you head out, since many of these are small shops that open only for part of the day.

items.name: Man Duay, behind Hat Yai train station
items.blurb: An old coconut-dessert stall that has been part of Hat Yai for over fifty years. They ladle sweet, fragrant coconut milk over shaved ice and let you add toppings like red beans, mashed taro, and candied pineapple. A lot of locals grew up on this one. Open midday to evening.

items.name: Pi Daeng Tub Tim Krob
items.blurb: Big, chewy water-chestnut pieces drowned in fragrant fresh coconut milk. Reviews praise how fresh the coconut milk is and how generous the water-chestnut size is. Eaten cold on a hot day, it hits the spot.

items.name: Old-school shaved ice, Thai Arkan intersection
items.blurb: A tiny stall by the traffic light at the Thai Arkan intersection, with shaved ice at twenty baht a bowl. You pick your own toppings — grass jelly, basil seeds, lod chong, black beans, candied taro. Old-style shaved ice at an easy price.
items.meta: Thai Arkan intersection · Shaved ice & grass jelly · From ฿20

items.name: Black sesame dumplings in ginger broth (with ginkgo)
items.blurb: Thin-skinned, soft-and-chewy rice dumplings in hot ginger broth, with ginkgo nuts added for a sweet, nutty touch. Good in the evening when it cools down a bit. Reviews praise the dumpling skin for being just the right softness.

items.name: Mae Luean Bua Loy (across from Thidanukroh School)
items.blurb: An old-timer coconut bua loy that people in the area have eaten for years. Soft dumplings, fresh coconut milk sweetened just right — a homey, made-fresh coconut dessert.
items.meta: Across from Thida School · Coconut bua loy · Around ฿30–40

items.name: Mae Fad Kluay Tub (Sao Thong area)
items.blurb: Grilled, flattened bananas topped with coconut milk and palm sugar, smoky from the grill and eaten with salty-sweet coconut. It's a Southern dessert that's getting harder to find.
items.meta: Sao Thong area · Grilled banana with coconut · Around ฿40–50

items.name: Siam Thai Fruit Icecream (behind Lotus)
items.blurb: Homemade fruit ice cream with natural flavors at thirty-five baht a scoop, with Thai toppings to choose from. Good for cooling off without being too sweet. It's behind Lotus.

items.name: Kala Fresh Coconut Ice Cream
items.blurb: Fresh-coconut ice cream served in a coconut shell, with Thai toppings like sticky rice, peanuts, and lod chong. A cold coconut dessert that tastes like real coconut.
items.meta: Market area · Coconut ice cream · Around ฿40–60

items.name: Me melon
items.blurb: Dense, smooth kakigori-style shaved ice with several flavors to choose from. The price is a bit higher because it's a newer style of shaved ice focused on a soft texture, starting around ninety-five baht. Good for anyone who likes fine, bingsu-style ice.
items.meta: In town · Kakigori shaved ice · From ฿95

items.name: Arunee Original Thai Dessert
items.blurb: A traditional Thai sweets shop with foi thong, thong yip, and made-fresh Thai desserts. Good for anyone who wants real Thai sweets or something to take home as a gift.
items.meta: In town · Traditional Thai sweets · Per piece

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Fresh-coconut sweets like man duay and bua loy are usually made day-of and sell out before evening. If you've got your eye on a particular shop, go in the early afternoon to be safe rather than waiting until after dark.

blocks.text: Fresh-coconut sweets — the style Hat Yai does well

blocks.html: If you had to pick one dessert style to try in Hat Yai, we'd push you toward the fresh-coconut sweets, because many shops still press their own coconut milk and make it day-of. The flavor is rich and fragrant in a way boxed coconut milk just isn't. Tub tim krob, bua loy, and coconut ice cream are the three that are easy to find and hard to mess up.

items.name: Tub tim krob
items.blurb: Water chestnut in a crisp flour coating, in cold fresh coconut milk. A popular cool-down dessert you'll find at almost every market.

items.name: Coconut bua loy
items.blurb: Soft rice dumplings in sweet, rich coconut milk. Some shops add a sweet egg or hot ginger broth.

items.name: Coconut ice cream
items.blurb: Ice cream made with real coconut, served with Thai toppings in a coconut shell or a bowl, with genuine coconut flavor.

blocks.text: Southern khanom jeen — a light meal or a snack, your call

blocks.html: Hat Yai khanom jeen isn't a dessert, but it's a city staple that many people eat for breakfast or a light lunch. The draw is the rich Southern curry sauces, strong on the curry paste, eaten with a plate of fresh raw vegetables on the side. Some shops serve fried chicken alongside. These are the ones reviews mention most.

items: Pa Chuen Khanom Jeen (several branches in Hat Yai) — several sauces to choose from, including green chicken curry and tai pla curry, eaten with fried chicken. It's a frequently recommended spot with pretty good reviews.
Luang Thip Fresh Noodle Khanom Jeen — focused on freshly made khanom jeen noodles served by the tray, with several Southern sauces to choose from, especially the strong tai pla curry.
Ko Piak Khanom Jeen (in front of Sena Narong Camp) — big plates of khanom jeen soaked in plenty of sauce, with bold Southern curry paste. Reviews praise how rich the sauce is.
Khanom Jeen Tao Khua, by the public park — has both coconut-milk khanom jeen and green curry, in an easy-to-reach spot near the municipal public park.
Lung Khai Pak Phanang Khanom Jeen, Songkhla — several sauces to choose from, including nam ya, tai pla curry, and green curry. Properly Southern, for anyone who likes bold flavors.

blocks.title: Eating Southern khanom jeen well
blocks.html: Southern nam ya and tai pla curry are quite a bit bolder than the central-Thai versions. If you're not used to it, order the coconut-milk nam ya first, then work your way up to tai pla curry — and don't skip the raw vegetables, since the fresh greens do a good job cutting the heat.

blocks.text: Planning a Hat Yai dessert run without overdoing it

blocks.html: Hat Yai desserts are spread across several neighborhoods, so mapping them into a route lets you eat more comfortably than hitting them at random. We've sketched out two days following the rhythm locals actually eat by — adjust it to your hotel and the shops' hours.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Coconut and shaved ice around the city center

items.activity: Start at man duay behind the train station
items.note: The shop opens at noon — go early before it sells out. Order coconut milk over shaved ice with all the toppings.

items.activity: Then the old-school shaved ice at Thai Arkan intersection
items.note: Twenty baht a bowl — pick grass jelly and lod chong to cool off in the afternoon.

items.activity: Finish with Pi Daeng tub tim krob or coconut ice cream
items.note: Cold fresh coconut before heading back to your hotel — not too heavy on the stomach.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Southern khanom jeen for breakfast, then Thai sweets

items.activity: Pa Chuen Khanom Jeen or Luang Thip fresh-noodle khanom jeen
items.note: Start with the coconut-milk nam ya, then try the tai pla curry, and pile on the raw vegetables.

items.activity: Coconut bua loy or black sesame dumplings in ginger broth
items.note: A light dessert after breakfast — pick the warm or cold version depending on the weather.

items.activity: Stop by a traditional Thai sweets shop for gifts
items.note: Foi thong or made-fresh Thai sweets you can take home as a gift.

faq.q: What Hat Yai desserts should you try?
faq.a: The ones people mention most are the fresh-coconut man duay behind the train station that has been around for over fifty years, fresh-coconut tub tim krob, and old-school shaved ice with grass jelly. For something properly Southern, the nam ya khanom jeen works as a light meal.

faq.q: Where's good for shaved ice and grass jelly in Hat Yai?
faq.a: The old-school shaved ice around the Thai Arkan intersection is the easy-on-the-wallet pick, with bowls starting at twenty baht and your own choice of toppings — grass jelly, basil seeds, lod chong. If you prefer the smooth, kakigori-style ice, try Me melon in town, which starts around ninety-five baht.

faq.q: Which Southern khanom jeen shops in Hat Yai are good?
faq.a: Pa Chuen Khanom Jeen, with several branches, is frequently recommended and serves fried chicken alongside. If you like bold flavors, try Ko Piak Khanom Jeen in front of Sena Narong Camp, or Luang Thip fresh-noodle khanom jeen, which focuses on fresh noodles and tai pla curry.

faq.q: Roughly how much do Hat Yai fresh-coconut desserts cost?
faq.a: Most are in the rough range of 25–60 baht a bowl. Tub tim krob and coconut bua loy run around 30–40 baht, man duay starts around 25 baht, and coconut or fruit ice cream is around 35–60 baht. Easy on the wallet.

faq.q: What hours are Hat Yai dessert shops open?
faq.a: Fresh-coconut shops like man duay usually open midday to evening and sell out fast. Khanom jeen shops open morning to afternoon, while shaved ice and ice cream can stay open into the evening. We'd suggest checking opening hours in a maps app before you go, since many are small shops that open only for part of the day.
